title: Image Registration Protocol for Correlative Soft X-ray Tomography and Super-Resolution Microscopy
author: Vyas, Kunne, et al.

steps.title: Load SIR data into Chromagnon
steps.instruction: Add the SIR data (for 2‑channel files) to both the Reference and Target fields in Chromagnon; if each fluorescence channel is in a separate file, add one as the ‘Target’ and the other as the ‘Source’.

steps.title: Execute Chromagnon alignment
steps.instruction: Press “Run all” to start the alignment.

steps.title: Assess alignment result
steps.instruction: Visually evaluate the automatic display generated by Chromagnon; the fluorescence signal should align well in all dimensions.

steps.title: Obtain reference matrix file
steps.instruction: Request the appropriate “chromagnon.csv” reference file from the microscope facility or beamline support scientists.

steps.title: Select and load reference file
steps.instruction: Choose the reference file that matches the laser wavelength and filter used for imaging your sample and add it to the ‘Reference’ field in Chromagnon.

steps.title: Load SIR data as source
steps.instruction: Add the SIR data to be aligned into the ‘Source’ field.

steps.title: Set output format and name
steps.instruction: In the Target panel, set the suffix to “.dv”; the output file will be created as “_ALN.dv”. After alignment, save the corrected SIR image for chromatic shift as “_ALN.tif”.

steps.title: Run Chromagnon with reference
steps.instruction: Press “Run all” to apply the reference‑based alignment.

steps.title: Check alignment outcome
steps.instruction: Visually evaluate the result; fluorescence signal should align well across the volume.

steps.title: Batch‑process multiple images
steps.instruction: Place all SIR images to be aligned in the Source field, add the same reference file in the Reference field, and press “Run all” to process them together.

description: Advances in imaging technology are constantly enabling breakthroughs in biological sub-cellular research. Cryo-imaging, specifically, allows for nanometer resolution at near-physiological conditions (Henderson et al., 1990) and correlative cryo-imaging integrates further information about cellular processes. A recent development in correlative cryo-imaging involves a platform developed at the correlative cryo-imaging beamline B24 at the UK synchrotron facility which combines 3D super resolution fluorescence microscopy (cryo-SIM) (Phillips et al., 2020) and soft X-ray tomography (cryo-SXT) (Kounatidis et al., 2020) (Figure 1).Figure 1Illustration of correlative imaging of an area of a cell combining cryo-SIM and cryo-SXT. Image data from reovirus infected U2OS cells as described in Kounatidis et al. (2020)The grayscale orthoslices show representative X-ray-generated contrast of cellular vesicles (part of the nucleus can be seen on the bottom right with endosomes clearly delineated in the surrounding cytoplasm). Green volumes are representations of Alexa-488 green fluorescent reovirus localization within endosomes identified by endovesicular concentrations of mCherry-tagged red-fluorescent galectin-3. A crucial step in the analysis of imaging data generated across microscopes within an imaging platform is the accurate image co-registration without systematic positional errors or data distortion in 3D. Here we demonstrate the use of the open source Icy (De Chaumont et al., 2012) plugin eC-CLEM (Paul-Gilloteaux et al., 2017) for the registration of SIM and SXT data. eC-CLEM was developed originally for correlating light and electron microscopy images and we present here protocols that allow its adoption for the registration of light microscopy and X-ray tomography volumes in an easy to follow step-by-step process.
